legend: You are given an array a$$$a$$$ consisting of n$$$n$$$ integers. Each ai$$$a_i$$$ is one of the six following numbers: 4,8,15,16,23,42$$$4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42$$$.
Your task is to remove the minimum number of elements to make this array good.
An array of length k$$$k$$$ is called good if k$$$k$$$ is divisible by 6$$$6$$$ and it is possible to split it into k6$$$\frac{k}{6}$$$ subsequences 4,8,15,16,23,42$$$4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42$$$.
[4,8,15,16,23,42]$$$[4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42]$$$ (the whole array is a required sequence);

[4,8,4,15,16,8,23,15,16,42,23,42]$$$[4, 8, 4, 15, 16, 8, 23, 15, 16, 42, 23, 42]$$$ (the first sequence is formed from first, second, fourth, fifth, seventh and tenth elements and the second one is formed from remaining elements);

[4,8,15,16,23,42,4,8,15,16,23,23]$$$[4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42, 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 23]$$$ (the first sequence can be formed from first six elements but the remaining array cannot form the required sequence).
input: The first line of the input contains one integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤5⋅105$$$1 \le n \le 5 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of elements in a$$$a$$$.

The second line of the input contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ (each ai$$$a_i$$$ is one of the following numbers: 4,8,15,16,23,42$$$4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42$$$), where ai$$$a_i$$$ is the i$$$i$$$-th element of a$$$a$$$.
output: Print one integer — the minimum number of elements you have to remove to obtain a good array.
